judged_text: The restructured expandable_first_post? tests still treat embeddable hosts as a gating input even though this diff removed the host check from the method: the 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false and has_topic_embed? is false on a built topic, and every positive test fabricates an EmbeddableHost the code never reads. The suite cannot detect a regression that re-introduces a host requirement into expandable_first_post? (all positive cases have a host present and the 'blank host' case passes for unrelated reasons), and a reader of the spec concludes hosts still gate the behavior when the code now ignores them entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checks embeddable hosts (`SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` was removed), but `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` still contains a top-level example named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" and a nested context that fabricates `:embeddable_host` even though the method under test no longer reads that model/setting. The "blank host" example no longer sets `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` or `has_topic_embed?`, so it can pass for unrelated default reasons, and all positive cases fabricate an `EmbeddableHost`, meaning the spec wouldn’t catch a regression that reintroduced a host gate. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test-quality/coverage issue rather than a runtime defect.
